description: The bar chart titled "QLoRA" compares the number of floating-point operations (FLOPs) required by different fine-tuning methods for a language model on multiple datasets. The vertical axis is labeled "# FLOPs" and is on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^18 to 10^20. The horizontal axis lists six different fine-tuning methods: Full FT, TAG, Lora, MTL-FT, QLoRA, and Ours. The bars are colored in shades of orange, with the exception of the last bar representing "Ours," which is green. The Full FT method requires the most FLOPs, indicated by the tallest bar, while the "Ours" method requires the least, as shown by the shortest bar. The values for each method are not explicitly provided, but the relative heights of the bars suggest that the "Ours" method is significantly more efficient in terms of computation cost compared to the other methods.
